title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Tea Party on 1969-12-31
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the legendary NYE ’69 show with smoking performances of Black Peter, The Eleven and Alligator, plus rare gems like Big Boy Pete.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD restoration delivers a vivid, almost “you‑are‑there” listening experience that many fans describe as comparable to an official release.  The concert is packed with high‑energy moments—standout renditions of Black Peter, The Eleven, Alligator and the rare Big Boy Pete—while the band’s chemistry feels pure psychedelic fire.  A few minor quirks (slight speed/pitch variance and a tiny cut smoothed by Miller) are noted, but they do not detract from the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.86/5 with overwhelming praise for both performance and sound quality; only one mixed review tempers the score slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix that feels like a modern GD release; occasional slight speed/pitch variance noted and a brief cut at ~11:08 smoothed in the Miller source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑set NYE show with a jam‑heavy second set; the flow is tight and the rare tracks add excitement, making the concert feel like a cohesive, high‑energy experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work gets constant shout‑outs – his tone on China Cat Sunflower, Alligator and the smoky soloing throughout are described as killer.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is praised for nonstop jam power (‘Phil bombs’) and driving the transition into The Eleven with a fierce bass line.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals are highlighted as honest and strong (e.g., on Mama Tried) and his rhythm work keeps the groove solid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard/organ presence noted – ‘Pig organ’ sounds robust, and the overall keyboard texture adds to the psychedelic vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s cannon‑like fill on Caution is singled out; drum work generally supports the high‑energy feel.
